what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 4: Is there a LOCAL rule under which inertial streaming keeps the rule's law stationary?. SETTING (block 50; open PR titled 'ail50: inertia joined with the rule's pair weights by a clock'): six-axis menu on a periodic cubic window; a configuration is a set of occupied sites with one of six contents each (contents 0..5 = +x, -x, +y, -y, +z, -z); the law with vacancies gives it the weight pi(C) = product over adjacent occupied pairs of c omega(a, b), omega = p for equal contents, q for opposite, r for orthogonal ((p, q, r) = (3, 1, 2) is the campaign's reference, c = 1 or the neutral scale c_0 = 6/(p + q + 4r)). Inertial streaming (block 44): the record at x with content s has the target x + e_s; an empty target is entered; an occupied target exchanges contents with the record. ESTABLISHED: every record has exactly one event and exactly one predecessor (the same record one site back if the site behind is empty, the two contents exchanged back if it is occupied), so with every event of C at the rate 1/pi(C) (GLOBAL clock) pi is stationary for any weights and density; with the event of the record at x at the rate 1/pi_x(C) (LOCAL clock; pi_x = product of the pair weights of site x) the balance defect is out - in = sum over records whose site behind b is occupied (content u) of W_0 [A_b(u) - A_x(u)], zero for two records and non-zero at three (3168 of the 70200 three-record configurations with a record at the origin on the 3x3x3 torus; largest 3 at (0,0,0):+y, (0,0,1):+z, (0,1,0):+y). Exact code: the block's runner scripts/admissibility_rule_inertia_joined_with_the_rules_pair_weights_by_a_clock_*.py and specs/supervisor_control_block50_refuter.py on the PR branch. TASK: decide it on the three-record sector, then say what generalizes. (a) Set up the linear feasibility problem: unknown non-negative rates for every event (a move into an empty target; an exchange of contents with an occupied target), where a rate may depend only on the contents and occupancies of the sites within distance one of the two sites of the event, modulo the lattice symmetries that fix the event (covariance). Constraints: for every three-record configuration of the 3x3x3 torus, the flow of pi in equals the flow out; moves must have positive rates. Solve it exactly (rational arithmetic; an LP solver may propose, exact arithmetic must verify) for (p, q, r) = (3, 1, 2) at c = 1 and at c_0 = 1/2. (b) If feasible: exhibit the rule in closed form if you can, check it at four records on a sample, and say whether number and momentum are still conserved event by event. (c) If infeasible: give a certificate (a dual vector), and then enlarge the family: allow an additional momentum-conserving event when the target is occupied (for instance both records keep their contents and nothing happens, or the pair re-draws its contents on its momentum class), and repeat. (d) State the result as a theorem with its scope. check.py: exact verification of the balance at every three-record configuration for the rule or the certificate you give.  DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/local-clock-for-inertia-with-weights/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/local-clock-for-inertia-with-weights/<name>/check.py"
